title: Static SDF AO closer to ray-traced ground truth, at most 4 texture reads per pixel
additional_information:
Improve the accuracy of a screen-free ambient occlusion formula. The function to edit is `ao(n, wall, sample)` in accuracy/ao_formula.py. Its docstring states the interface and the rules, which the judge enforces before running it.

What it computes: per visible pixel of a 1280x720 render of a static scene (159 axis-aligned boxes: floor, two walls, stairs, shelves, crates), the ambient visibility in [0, 1]. The judge compares it with a ray-traced reference: 512 cosine-weighted rays per pixel, a hit counting as occluded within 1.12 m. The score is the mean absolute error over each camera view's pixels; three views are visible to the judge's cells and three more are held out.

What the formula sees: the surface normal, a flag for the two large structural walls, and `sample(offset)`, the trilinearly interpolated signed distance to the scene (half-float 128^3 volume over a 26 x 18 x 8 m box, voxels about 20 x 14 x 6 cm, clipped at +1.5 m, negative inside) at the pixel's surface point plus an offset. At most 4 sample calls: each is one 3D texture read in the GLSL shader the formula is ported to, so the per-pixel cost stays the same. It does not see positions or the scene layout.

The seed is the shipped 'SDF wall correction' formula: 4 taps along the normal at 0.16 / 0.48 / 0.80 / 1.12 m, occlusion clamp(1 - (d + 0.045) / r), weighted, with weights shifted toward the near taps on structural walls to stop them over-darkening. Its MAE: 0.0401 on the main view; 0.025-0.050 across views.

Hard limits: at most 4 samples, and no more over-darkening on structural walls than the seed (mean of max(0, reference - ao) over wall pixels). The held-out views must not get worse.

The winning formula will be ported by hand to GLSL, so keep it to arithmetic a fragment shader can do in a few lines.
ideas: Tap placement: different radii, or offsets tilted away from the normal (a small cone) to see occluders beside the surface rather than straight above it
Nonlinear distance-to-occlusion response per tap (smoothstep, a power) instead of the linear clamp
Combine taps multiplicatively (product of per-tap visibilities) or with a soft maximum, instead of a weighted sum
Treat floors (n.z near 1), walls (wall flag) and other vertical faces differently
Use the sign and size of the nearest-tap distance to detect concave corners and contact regions
